items.title: 特朗普據報將赴機場迎接習近平，待遇比肩教宗和赫魯曉夫
items.description: 美國總統親赴機場迎接外國元首極為罕見。若不計教宗訪美的特例，這將是超過 60 年來美國總統首次以這種方式迎接他國元首。
items.content:
特朗普據報將赴機場迎接習近平，待遇比肩教宗和赫魯曉夫：回顧兩國外交禮賓細節
路透社、彭博社等多家通訊社報導，一名美國高級官員週五（9月18日）向記者透露，美國總統特朗普（Donald Trump；川普）計劃下週親赴華盛頓郊外的安德魯斯聯合基地（Joint Base Andrews），迎接前來進行國事訪問的中國國家主席習近平。
國事訪問的禮賓程序高度程式化，但程式之中仍留有彈性空間，足以傳遞微妙的政治信號。東道國接機官員的級別，歷來是觀察雙邊關係溫度最直接的風向標。
美國總統親赴機場迎接外國元首極為罕見。若不計教宗訪美的特例，這將是超過 60 年來美國總統首次以這種方式迎接他國元首。
這一決定發生在中美關係仍處於貿易摩擦和科技競爭陰影之下的時刻，其象徵意義因此格外受到關注。以下從歷史先例、中美互動禮賓變化，以及習近平近年出訪所獲接待規格三個層面，梳理這次安排背後的外交邏輯。
美國總統機場迎賓：歷史上有多罕見
美國總統親赴機場迎接來訪元首，並非從未發生，但案例集中在特定年代。
肯尼迪總統圖書館的資料顯示，1960年代，時任總統肯尼迪（John F. Kennedy）曾多次親自到安德魯斯空軍基地迎接來訪的外國元首，迎接對象包括加納總統恩克魯瑪（Kwame Nkrumah）、突尼斯總統布爾吉巴（Habib Bourguiba）、秘魯總統普拉多（Manuel Prado）、厄瓜多爾總統阿羅塞梅納（Carlos Julio Arosemena）、幾內亞總統塞古·杜爾（Ahmed Sékou Touré）、以及印度總理尼赫魯（Jawaharlal Nehru）等。
但與現在不同的是，肯尼迪執政初期，與其說去接機，其實是因為把歡迎儀式直接放在機場舉行。
在肯尼迪執政後期，頻繁穿越華盛頓迎到機場迎接，時常造成交通擁堵，所以他就改革了這個禮賓儀式，正式確定白宮南草坪為外賓抵達的正式歡迎舞台。此後，外賓飛抵安德魯斯空軍基地之後，由禮賓司長接機並乘直升飛機直抵白宮，再由總統在南草坪舉行歡迎儀式。這成為了美國的外交慣例。
因此，更有可比性的是1959年，時任總統艾森豪威爾（Dwight D. Eisenhower）親自到安德魯斯空軍基地，在舷梯下迎接蘇聯最高領導人赫魯曉夫（Nikita Khrushchev）。而且這在當時也被事先公開和廣泛報道，被視為冷戰下微妙且罕見的禮遇。
不過近年來，在禮賓安排上，羅馬天主教教宗是例外：1987年，里根（Ronald Reagan）在邁阿密機場迎接教宗若望保祿二世（Pope John Paul II）；1999 年，克林頓（Bill Clinton）在機場迎接再次迎接教宗若望保祿二世（Pope John Paul II）；2008年，小布什（George W. Bush）夫婦在安德魯斯空軍基地迎接教宗本篤十六世（Pope Benedict XVI）；2015年，奧巴馬（Barack Obama）夫婦在安德魯斯聯合基地迎接教宗方濟各（Pope Francis）。
過去11年間，再無教宗訪美。
與中方接待特朗普的規格相比
白宮傳出的消息若果屬實，則美方此次安排，規格已超過中方今年5月接待特朗普時的水平。當時特朗普抵達北京，到機場迎接的是國家副主席、前中共中央政治局常委韓正。
特朗普第一任期訪華時，接機人是時任中共中央政治局委員、國務委員楊潔篪。楊潔篪當時在中國外事領域擁有實際決策權，屬於「黨和國家領導人」序列，規格已屬較高。
美國總統在中方接待序列中，歷來享有比一般外國首腦更高的禮遇。多數外國元首訪華時，接機官員通常為部長級，例如德國總理默茨（Friedrich Merz）、英國首相斯塔默（Keir Starmer）訪華時，分別由外交部副部長和財政部長接機。
值得一提的是，根據白宮向記者們透露的行程顯示，習近平的夫人彭麗媛將陪同他一起訪問美國，也算是釋放友善信號，因為在5月份特朗普訪華時，夫人梅拉尼婭·特朗普（Melania Trump）並未隨行。
中國如何接待外國領導人
俄羅斯總統普京（Vladimir Putin）訪華時，享有與美國總統類似級別的接待。今年5月，由中共中央政治局委員、外交部長王毅接機；2025年8月赴天津出席上海合作組織峰會時，則由政治局委員、中共天津市委書記陳敏爾接機。
朝鮮最高領導人金正恩訪華時，曾由中共中央政治局常委王滬寧親自迎接，七常委之一出面接機極為罕見。但這一待遇延續的是中朝之間源自冷戰年代的同盟式「兄弟情誼」，並不屬於中國對外接待的常規序列。
在常規外交框架之外，歷史上有兩次美國總統訪華所獲接待規格超過了普京和金正恩。1972年尼克松（Richard Nixon）「破冰之旅」訪華，當時中美尚未建交，國務院總理周恩來親赴機場迎接，規格之高至今未被超越。
另一次是2009年奧巴馬首次訪華，接機的是時任國家副主席習近平。彼時習近平身兼中共中央政治局常委與國家副主席，且已被公認為接班人，這一安排被普遍視為超規格禮遇。
到了奧巴馬第二任期，美國推出「亞洲再平衡」戰略，中美關係出現波折，接機人選隨即降為外交部長王毅。接機人選的升降，由此成為觀察中美關係走向的晴雨表之一。
習近平經歷過的領導人接機
近年來，習近平出訪時獲外國領導人親自接機，已不算罕見事件。
最近一次是今年6月8日訪問朝鮮時，金正恩親自到機場迎接。這延續了中國領導人訪朝的傳統：此前胡錦濤、江澤民出訪朝鮮，乃至更早年代周恩來以總理身份訪朝時，均由朝鮮最高領導人親自到機場迎接。
其他國家由元首親赴機場迎接習近平的情況也時有發生，但通常需滿足兩個條件：一是與中國關係密切，二是國家體量較小。2024年習近平訪問塞爾維亞時，總統武契奇（Aleksandar Vučić）到停機坪迎接；同年訪問匈牙利時，總理歐爾班（Viktor Orbán）到機場迎接；2025年訪問柬埔寨時，國王西哈莫尼（Norodom Sihamoni）在機場迎接。
更早的一個特殊案例發生在2014年7月。習近平在赴巴西出席金磚國家領導人峰會途中，在希臘羅德島作技術經停。技術經停通常只涉及加油和短暫休整，並不安排正式外交活動。然而希臘時任總統帕普利亞斯（Karolos Papoulias）與總理薩馬拉斯（Antonis Samaras）專程從雅典飛赴羅德島，在機場迎接習近平並舉行會談。兩國最高領導人跨城出迎一次過境停留，極為罕見。
這次超規格接待，背景是希臘當時仍深陷歐債危機，經濟和就業形勢嚴峻，又受到國際紓困計劃的嚴厲財政約束，急需外來投資和基礎設施項目支撐復甦。習近平此行距他提出「一帶一路」倡議僅約十個月。此次會晤後，中希兩國經貿合作明顯提速：兩年後的2016年，中遠海運取得比雷埃夫斯港運營商的控股權，並持續加大對該港口的開發投入。
國際通訊社透露的習近平訪美行程一覽
9月23日（週三）
習近平及夫人彭麗媛抵達安德魯斯聯合基地。
特朗普親赴機場迎接，雙方在該軍事基地舉行抵達歡迎儀式，這在安德魯斯聯合基地同樣極為少見。
9月24日（週四）：會談與國宴
特朗普將在白宮迎接習近平與彭麗媛。
雙方隨後移步玫瑰園，進行儀仗檢閱，再展開雙邊會談。
梅拉尼婭·特朗普與彭麗媛將出席在華盛頓地區舉行的另一場活動，白宮尚未公布具體細節。
晚間，特朗普夫婦將在白宮東廳為習近平與彭麗媛舉辦國宴。特朗普與習近平將在晚宴開始時分別致辭，出席嘉賓包括科技與金融界高管。
9月25日（週五）：茶敘、參觀與離境
特朗普夫婦將在白宮為習近平與彭麗媛舉辦茶敘。
雙方隨後前往華盛頓國家檔案館，參觀美國建國文獻。
習近平與彭麗媛啟程返回安德魯斯聯合基地，隨後離境。

items.title: 當白宮舉行宴會時，台灣會出現在「菜單」上嗎？
items.description: 日媒稱美中峰會前，白宮若批准新的對台軍售，習近平可能不去華府。對台灣的軍售從原則如何變成交易槓桿，台灣的晶片牌仍然有效嗎？
items.content:
習近平訪美前瞻：當白宮舉行宴會時，台灣會出現在「菜單」上嗎？
  - Author, 呂嘉鴻
  - Role, BBC 中文
- Published
- 閱讀時間: 4 分鐘
中美兩國元首本月稍晚預定在華府舉行的「特習會」，是全球矚目的外交焦點，但截至目前，沒有人能公開確認習近平是否真的會踏上美國國土。原因之一，是各方熟知的台灣問題。
據日本共同社上週末（12日）報道，多名熟悉中美關係的消息人士稱，北京已告知華府：若美方在會談前批准任何一筆新的百億美元級對台軍售案，中方有意取消這場原定於本月下旬舉行的峰會。儘管特朗普（Donald Trump）已公開表示，將於9月24日在白宮接待習近平夫婦並舉行國宴，但中國官方至今仍未正式宣布訪美行程。
這一報道引發外界關注：中美圍繞台灣問題的互動，是否已進入一個新階段?北京似乎不再滿足於重申原則性表態，而是把包括軍售在內的台灣議題，代入特朗普「交易式」外交風格。
英國諾丁漢大學（University of Nottingham）中國研究學院院長、當代中國研究副教授蘇利文（Jonathan Sullivan）向BBC中文表示：「我們並不是說特朗普心裡有一筆關於台灣的大交易，絕對不是這個意思。但如果他的動機是要拿到『一場勝利』，那麼他為此可能動用的選項，比前任美國總統更多，當然，這在很大程度上取決於中國施壓的力度。」
中美進入交易模式？
從北京與白宮的斡旋來看，台灣依然是北京口中不容觸碰的「紅線」，但操作手法確實變得更加交易化。據共同社報道，特朗普急於在11月中期選舉前交出一份外交成績單，因此極為重視這場峰會。中國正是抓住這一點，把「習近平是否赴美」變成一項籌碼。
北京傳遞的核心訊息，其實與5月特朗普訪京後的官方表態並無二致：台灣是中美關係「最重要的問題」，處理不好「就會發生碰撞甚至衝突」。但9月的不同之處在於，這一次不是峰會後的事後警告，而是在會面前就把軍售議題直接攤上檯面。
新加坡南洋理工大學（NTU）副教授駱明輝向BBC中文分析稱，若說中國對美戰略已經「根本性轉變」為交易模式，恐怕還言之過早。
「雖然北京確實更往交易式做法靠攏，並試圖把『紅線』往軍售議題上挪，但北京擔心的是國際觀感，如果這筆對台軍售恰好在習近平身處華府期間拍板過關，畫面會非常難看，所以北京不太可能在這一點上賭運氣，與特朗普硬碰硬。」
蘇利文則指出，北京不會用「以物易物」的框架來公開表述任何關於台灣的討論，但各方都清楚中國要什麼，特朗普又需要什麼。
「中南海願望清單的首位，是美方明確表態『反對台灣獨立』，其次是進一步檢討已同意的對台軍售包裹。5月峰會之後，有一批軍售被暫緩，因此圍繞軍售的調整，看起來比較有操作空間。」
美國智庫德國馬歇爾基金會（GMF）印太計畫主任葛來儀（Bonnie Glaser）早在5月特朗普訪京後便向《紐約時報》分析，習近平認為存在機會，能讓美國「不只延後軍售，甚至縮減規模，或是長時間不再出售」。上週共同社報道傳出後，她在社交平台X上評論稱：「對台軍售會恢復，問題不是會不會，只是何時。未來兩週不太可能，峰會之後則有可能。」
布魯金斯學會中國中心主任何瑞恩（Ryan Hass）則從特朗普的談判手法切入分析。他曾尖銳評論，特朗普公開要求台北「冷靜」，等同向北京釋放了一個訊號：美國對台安全支持「是可以跟中國談的」。
他批評，這種公開的可談判性「就像鬥牛場裡的紅布，刺激著北京去試探美國承諾的邊界」。
換言之，這一新階段的出現，並非北京突然發明了新的紅線，而是華府主動把既有的紅線擺上了談判桌。
北京開始點菜：能用什麼換到什麼
蘇利文向BBC中文指出，中國在出口管制、關稅以及台灣問題上都有明確訴求，同時也握有一些可以包裝成特朗普「勝利」的籌碼，例如關鍵礦產出口、大豆進口，以及「對伊朗與俄羅斯發揮影響力」等。這使中國在談判中處於相對有利的位置，也讓其能夠開出更高的價碼。
中國研究網站《Sinification》報道，今年5月底，在特習北京會後的一場對台問題專家座談上，廈門大學教授李鵬承認特朗普難以預測，但認為兩位領袖之間反覆的互動，或許可以「穩住」這位美國總統，進而有助於兩岸與中美關係的整體穩定。
另一位與會的台灣問題專家，上海東亞研究所教授王海良則強調，北京必須善加利用未來三年，塑造中美台互動中「正向、不可逆」的趨勢，把華盛頓推向「非正式的光榮中立」，趁著這位「可塑性高」的美國總統仍在任上，「趕緊做工作」。
蘇利文同時強調，特朗普本身也擁有一項優勢，那就是他已經完全掌控自己的政黨，建立了一套不可預測卻又能全身而退的行事紀錄，也不受意識形態或政策一致性的束縛。
因此，「如果真要想像哪位總統會跟中國做這種交易，那就是特朗普。總的來說，中國目前處於相對有利的位置，可以再要更多。」
「但他們也清楚，一旦特朗普被逼到角落，可能做出不可預測、甚至傷害自身利益的舉動。」蘇利文說。
台灣位置被動，但不是無牌可打
此時此刻，台北正夾在中美之間的交易博弈，以及國內「朝小野大」的政治格局之中。今年5月，在野黨掌握的立法院，將原本規劃約1.25萬億新台幣的國防特別預算大幅削減至約7800億元，並刪除了部分國產與非對稱戰力項目。
美國軍事評論員艾克塞（David Axe）曾批評，這一削減等同砍掉了將台灣打造成「刺蝟島」的核心能力。近期立法院雖已通過無人載具相關條例，但朝野仍在採購方案與預算審核上持續拉鋸。
台灣獨立政治新聞網站「破土」主編、英國諾丁漢大學台灣研究中心客座研究員丘琦欣（Brian Hioe）向BBC中文分析：「特朗普似乎總想把自己塑造成『偉大交易』的撮合者。因此，對台北而言，賴清德總統的選擇空間其實相當有限，但他可以透過與其他美國國會議員的聯繫，間接向特朗普施壓，或是設法把最終結果包裝成一筆能歸功於特朗普本人的重大交易。」
「但更廣泛來說，特朗普似乎仍對台灣抱持一定敵意，並偏好與北京進行交易，即便他同時也展現出願意直接就對台軍售進行談判的態度，這是前任美國總統所沒有的做法。」丘琦欣補充道。
蘇利文則認為，賴清德總統目前能做的其實相當有限：台北已經把幾乎所有籌碼都押在美國身上，特朗普提出的要求，賴清德幾乎都已履行，現在只能等著看這能換來什麼結果。
台灣作為全球最重要的先進半導體生產基地、運作良好的自由民主典範，同時也是美國忠實的盟友。
梳理這三點，蘇利文認為，「後兩項特朗普大概不太在意，他真正在意的是晶片，這對台灣仍是一項有利因素。我們或許可以透過這次美中峰會，觀察民進黨『全力押注硬威懾、背靠美國』這一選擇最終會得到怎樣的回應。」
台灣國防安全研究院助理研究員鍾志東上週在台北一場會議上則強調，當前的中美關係可以用「短多長空」來理解。
他進一步解釋，台美關係必須放在中美關係的整體結構中看待：1979年，美國即便需要聯合中國共同抗衡蘇聯，也未曾接受北京要求停止對台軍售的訴求。因此，在當前中美戰略競爭持續升高的背景下，美國在對台軍售議題上向中國讓步的空間，實際上比過去更低。
「特習會前，美方大概率不會宣布大筆對台軍售案，但這並不代表美國正在對中國妥協。」
無論習近平最終是否成行，對台軍售議題都不會就此消失，只會轉入下一輪交易。北京把峰會當作槓桿，華府把軍售當作籌碼，台北則既要應付立法院內部的預算拉鋸，又要設法讓自己出現在「餐桌旁」，而不是「菜單上」。

items.title: 「運動員無法伸直雙腿睡覺」：日本亞運為何爆發住宿爭議？
items.description: 亞運選手將入住木製貨櫃屋或一艘意大利郵輪。韓國代表團批評，貨櫃屋宿舍水管漏水，且床舖太小，運動員甚至無法伸直雙腿睡覺。
items.content:
「運動員無法伸直雙腿睡覺」：日本亞運為何爆發住宿爭議？
  - Author, 郭悠（Koh Ewe）
- Published
- 閱讀時間: 2 分鐘
日本亞洲運動會將於週六（9月19日）開幕，住宿問題成為外界激烈批評的焦點。
其中，為數千名運動員而設的木製貨櫃屋，賽前被指漏水和床舖太小。
「身高超過兩米（6呎7吋）的運動員，甚至無法在床上把腿伸直，這實在不合理。」韓國籃球協會副會長鄭載龍（音譯Jung Jae-yong）說。
他向法新社形容，這些住宿設施是「歷來最差的」。
本屆賽事於名古屋市及愛知縣舉行，超過1.7萬名運動員及官員出席，比原先預計的人數多了2000人，過去數週以來外界都擔心床位不足。
漏水的貨櫃屋
木製貨櫃屋將容納約2000人，並設計為日後可重複用作災害疏散設施，但一直飽受批評。
韓國籃球隊一名成員上傳影片，顯示房間內有水管漏水及地面積水，並附上文字：「請幫幫我。」
上週名古屋遭遇破紀錄降雨並引發大範圍水災後，入住貨櫃屋的運動員亦曾短暫疏散。一些比賽場館亦傳出漏水情況。
籃球官員鄭載龍向法新社表示，其他參賽國家代表亦有相同住宿方面的憂慮。
印度當局甚至搭建了這些貨櫃屋的複製版本，讓本國運動員預先適應相關住宿環境。
亞運住宿事務負責人松雄裕太（Yuta Matsuo）向路透社表示，主辦方「充分了解各代表團提出的不滿及憂慮」，強調正「採取具體措施改善運動員的住宿環境」。
有別於奧運會通常設有專屬選手村，亞運的主辦單位選擇以臨時住宿設施安置參賽者。
除貨櫃屋外，另有4000至5000名參賽者將入住一艘意大利郵輪。該郵輪已於週二停靠名古屋，其餘與會人士則將入住酒店。
大會最初預計，將有1.5萬名運動員及官員參加本屆亞運會。但亞洲奧林匹克理事會於8月中旬表示，在新增結合足球與桌球元素的桌式足球（teqball）及板式網球（padel）項目後，參與人數將接近1.7萬人。
亞運組委會主席兼愛知縣知事大村秀章（Hideaki Omura）此前表示，當局原本只為1.5萬人編列預算，對於新增運動員「既沒有足夠人力，也沒有足夠預算作出必要安排」。
他說：「根本沒有地方讓他們住宿。如果他們仍希望前來，就必須自行安排。」
不過，上月主辦方與亞洲奧林匹克理事會表示，所有於7月截止日期前完成報名的「超過1.7萬名」運動員及官員，均已獲提供「符合亞運標準的住宿安排」。
聲明表示：「所有最後準備工作均按計劃進行，且進展順利。本屆亞運會有望成為數十年來最精彩的一屆。」
菲律賓奧林匹克委員會主席托倫蒂諾（Abraham Tolentino）向法新社表示，雖然所有菲律賓運動員都已獲安排床位，但部分官員及教練則入住「不同的酒店和Airbnb」。
本屆亞洲運動會將於週六（9月19日）正式揭幕，並於10月4日閉幕。目前，籃球及足球賽事已經展開。

items.title: 澳洲收緊移民政策：管制留學生、背包客，打擊「簽證跳轉」
items.description: 澳洲政府希望在2028年前，將海外淨移民人數降至22.5萬人。
items.content:
澳洲收緊移民政策：管制留學生、背包客，打擊「簽證跳轉」
  - Author, 拉娜·林（Lana Lam）
  - Reporting from, 悉尼（Sydney）
- Published
- 閱讀時間: 3 分鐘
澳洲政府宣布收緊移民政策，重點管制國際學生和背包客，並打擊所謂的「簽證跳轉者」（visa hoppers）。
外國學生今後將不得攜帶家屬赴澳，而希望延長居留的人士則必須選擇攻讀更高層級的學位資格。「打工度假簽證」（working holiday visa；工作假期簽證）也將引入抽籤制度。
澳洲內政部長伯克（Tony Burke）在週四（9月17日）發表題為「管理移民計劃的工作：誰到來、誰留下、誰離開」的演講，公布一系列改革措施。
他表示，雖然移民是澳洲的一項「優勢」，但仍需要維持「高度管控」。澳洲政府希望在2028年前，將海外淨移民人數降至22.5萬人。
打擊「簽證跳轉」
談及國際學生及畢業生簽證時，伯克表示：「我們將不再讓學生自動擁有攜帶家庭成員來澳的資格。」
他表示，已身在澳洲的外國學生，以及來自太平洋地區和東南亞國家的申請人將獲得豁免。此外，博士生仍可攜帶家屬，因為他們與本科生處於不同的人生階段。
至於學生簽證，他表示政府將打擊「簽證跳轉」（visa hopping）行為，也就是學生完成一項課程後，再申請另一項課程，而後者通常屬於較低等級的資格，有時甚至來自「不那麼正規的教育機構」。
伯克表示，若學生是為了攻讀更高層級資格，仍可獲准繼續留澳。例如完成學士學位後，再攻讀碩士學位。
打工度假簽證須抽籤
打工度假簽證（working holiday visa；工作假期簽證）也將有重大調整。
這類簽證允許18至30歲人士申請，普遍由背包客使用，也是澳洲農業部門的重要勞動力來源，他們可在澳洲工作12個月，並可申請延長至第二及第三年。
目前，簽證持有人必須在第一年於澳洲偏遠地區工作滿三個月，才能取得第二年簽證資格；其後還需再工作六個月，才能取得第三年簽證資格。
根據新措施，符合第二年簽證資格的人士必須參加抽籤，名額上限為4.5萬個，低於去年符合資格的5.7萬人。
第三年簽證的抽籤名額則限制為5,000個，低於去年符合資格的3.1萬人。
由於英澳自由貿易協定，英國打工度假人士不受這些新措施影響。
過去一年增30萬海外移民
澳洲統計局週四公布的最新數據顯示，截至2026年3月止的12個月內，澳洲人口增長1.4%，達到2,790萬人。
有關數字包括出生和死亡人口變化，以及29.21萬人的海外淨移民人數。
隨著生活成本持續上升、住房負擔能力下降，以及公共服務承受更大壓力，澳洲人口規模的討論持續升溫，移民問題仍是重要政治議題。
以反移民立場聞名的右翼民粹政黨「同一國家黨」（One Nation），近月支持度顯著上升。該黨本週稍早公布移民政策，建議在三年內削減75萬個臨時移民簽證。
該黨於今年5月贏得首個聯邦眾議院議席，同時主張將海外淨移民人數上限設為13萬人。伯克批評這一提議，表示有可能「重創澳洲經濟的部分領域」。
今年7月，澳洲政府推出新政策，優先處理在澳洲境內提交的家庭簽證申請，即申請人在遞交申請時已身處澳洲境內，而非在海外提出申請。
已在澳洲境內並申請永久居留簽證的技術移民，也較海外申請人獲得優先處理。
政府同時暫停來自24個國家的打工度假簽證申請，但英國不在此限。
協助新移民在澳洲安頓的國際安置服務機構（Settlement Services International）的維奧萊特・魯梅利奧蒂斯（Violet Roumeliotis）表示，有關移民的辯論愈來愈受到「短期政治考量，而非最有利於國家的事情」所主導。
她說：「針對國際學生家庭簽證所提出的改變，就是一個很好的例子。」
她補充道，這將使澳洲更難與其他國家競爭、吸引「未來的人才」。

items.title: 美國科技巨頭呼籲放緩AI發展速度——中國怎麼看？
items.description: 隨著人工智能以驚人的速度發展，一些業內最傑出的領導者已經警告了它可能帶來的潛在風險。然而，世界兩大人工智能超級大國——中美之間的激烈競爭，可能會讓應對這項威脅的努力變得更加複雜。
items.content:
美國科技巨頭呼籲放緩AI發展速度——中國怎麼看？
  - Author, 劉睿正
  - Role, BBC Global China Unit
  - Reporting from, 香港
 
  - Author, 托尼·韓（Tony Han）
  - Role, BBC Global China Unit
  - Reporting from, 倫敦
- Published
- 閱讀時間: 3 分鐘
人工智能（AI）發展日新月異，業內一些具影響力的領袖卻嚴厲警告說，要正視AI可能帶來的危機。
譬如，Anthropic執行長達裡奧·阿莫迪（Dario Amodei）認為人工智能的發展速度應該放緩，而兩家競爭對手的高層——OpenAI的薩姆·奧特曼（Sam Altman）和埃隆·馬斯克（Elon Musk）——也贊同他的觀點。
美國矽谷的一些人士甚至認為，人工智能有朝一日可能會導致人類滅絕。
然而，應對這些風險也因兩大人工智能大國中國和美國之間的激烈競爭，而變得複雜。
作為戰略競爭對手，中美經常從國家安全和經濟優勢的角度看待人工智能的發展，讓人懷疑兩國是否能夠促成實質合作。
「如果國際社會期望美中就這些問題展開對話並達成具有約束力的協議，那麼它這期望會落空，」奧斯陸和平研究所（PRIO）高級研究員伊拉里亞·卡羅扎博士（Ilaria Carrozza）說。
「在人類控制下的人工智能」
中國為人工智能制定了宏大計劃，設想未來這項技術將融入農業、醫療和軍事等社會和經濟的各個領域。
可是，北京長期以來也一直警惕人工智能帶來的風險。
早在2017年，政府就表示人工智能可能侵犯隱私、威脅社會穩定和挑戰國際關係準則。
此後幾年，中國要求對社群媒體上的人工智能生成內容進行標註，禁止未成年人使用人工智能虛擬伴侶，並禁止使用深度偽造技術傳播假訊息。
對此，香港城市大學教授曾敬涵向BBC表示，不像美國的政府機構和政策顧問，中國官方對「人工智能可接受的發展，有相當大的決定權」。
曾教授曾參與中美針對人工智能的非正式會談。
對於人工智能可能失控的風險，中國國家主席習近平7月在世界人工智能合作組織（WAICO）會議上表示，這項技術必須「始終處於人類控制之下」。
WAICO由中國倡議成立，致力於促進國際社會在人工智能治理領域的對話與合作。
中國網路監管機構中共中央網絡安全和信息化委員會辦公室（簡稱網信辦）在9月公布《人工智能安全治理框架3.0》，其中表示，須要對人工智能危害「人類生存發展的風險及時採取措施」。
可治理的技術？
儘管中國官方承認人工智能有可能脫離人類控制，但相較於美國，人工智能是否能夠危及人類存續，在中國，並非相關討論的核心議題。
北京認為，這只是政府在制定政策時須要應對的眾多問題之一。
曾教授表示：「中國的人工智能治理兼顧多個目標：支持經濟發展、管理技術和社會風險以及維護政治權威。」
劉少山博士是深圳市人工智能與機器人研究院的具身智能中心主任，他對此表示贊同：「在中國的討論往往更著重於可控性、濫用和社會後果，而在美國的討論則更多地集中在人工智能失控或人類滅絕等假設性情境上。」
雖然中國官員憂心人工智能帶來的風險，但他們也相信，在中國經濟成長放緩之際，人工智能將成為提振經濟的重要動力。
譬如，騰訊、阿里巴巴、百度和字節跳動等中國科技巨頭的人工智能模型，正與全球主要競爭對手一較高下。一些領先模型則來自零一萬物、深度求索（DeepSeek）、MiniMax、月之暗面和智譜等新創公司。
這些公司都沒有回應BBC的置評請求。
劉少山博士向BBC解釋，北京正力求在培育人工智能產業和管控相關風險之間取得平衡。
「這與主張停止發展人工智能是兩回事，」他說。
「誰贏了人工智能，誰就贏了。」
除了國內發展需求，北京也必須考量地緣政治因素。
美國總統特朗普（Donald Trump，川普）將人工智能發展描述為一場與中國的高風險競賽。
「我們在人工智能領域領先中國……坦白說，我希望保持這種領先地位，因為誰贏了人工智能，誰就贏了，」他曾說。
中國國家安全部長陳一新在9月發表於官方期刊的文章中，也從地緣政治的角度闡述人工智能的發展，稱其為「大國戰略博弈的新賽道」。
儘管呼籲放緩人工智能發展的呼聲主要來自美國業界人士而非政府官員，但地緣政治競爭使北京對此類呼籲保持警惕。
今年8月，就在阿莫迪發出人工智能風險警告前不久，中國官媒批評Anthropic的聯合創始人將他的公司與美國的地緣政治利益捆綁在一起。
中國央視運營的社交媒體帳號「玉淵譚天」發帖批評：「阿莫代伊（阿莫迪）的邏輯已經完成了兩次放大：從『我在做好事』，到『我替你決定』；從『我的國家在做好事』，到『所有不配合的都應該被限制』」。
阿莫迪近日呼籲放慢人工智能發展步伐後，再度招致中國官媒批評。官媒特別點名他曾主張阻礙中國在人工智能領域的發展。
儘管雙方互信不足，外界仍期待習近平與特朗普本月稍後在美國首都華盛頓舉行的峰會上，能夠就部分議題達成共識。路透社報導，中方官員將人工智能視為峰會的重要議程。
對此，PRIO的卡羅札博士則向BBC表示，防範非國家行為者濫用人工智能和人工智能驅動的網絡攻擊威脅關鍵基礎設施等議題，或許能讓中美雙方建立一定程度的共識。然而，針對人工智能的發展步調達成明確協議，恐怕仍遙不可及。
她說：「較有可能透過雙邊協商處理的，大概是那些即使達成協議，也不須要驗證執行情況或揭露商業機密的議題。」
她同時指出，「至於限制任何一方開發人工智能模型速度的措施，美中雙方不太可能達成共識。」
本文原以英文撰寫，我們使用了人工智能協助翻譯，並由BBC記者在發佈前進行審核。了解更多關於我們如何使用人工智能的資訊。

items.title: 天皇宣布亚运会开幕  赛前折腾名古屋叫苦
items.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/天皇宣布亚运会开幕-赛前折腾名古屋叫苦/a-79339185?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
items.description: 第20届亚洲运动会周六在名古屋拉开帷幕。这场参赛规模宏大的体育盛会赛前却风波不断，令名古屋组织方应接不暇。亚洲各国各怀喜忧，各路新秀也将在此竞相绽放。因为天气原因和排名靠后，中国女子板球队还未上场即被淘汰回家。
items.content:
天皇宣布亚运会开幕 赛前折腾名古屋叫苦
2026年9月19日
（德国之声中文网）第20届亚洲运动会周六（9月19日）由日本天皇宣布开幕。这场参赛运动员人数超过奥运会的综合性体育盛会，筹备阶段一直麻烦缠身。
名古屋这座可容纳3万人的体育场内出现大量空座，气氛平淡的观众观看了一场在心形舞台上举行的、色彩缤纷的开幕式。
日本天皇与皇后入座时受到恭敬的迎接，国际奥委会主席考文垂（Kirsty Coventry）与他们同席。德仁天皇宣布本届运动会开幕时，场内响起礼节性的掌声。
首枚金牌将于周日上午产生，很可能出自男子个人铁人三项。亚洲最优秀的运动员将在40多个项目中角逐，赛事于10月4日落幕。
住宿告急 暴雨台风添乱
这项在名古屋和爱知县举行的赛事，有七个项目设有2028年奥运会参赛资格，届时将有世界级明星和迅速崛起的少年天才登场。
但赛前它一直问题不断：超过1.1万名运动员和6000名官员让组织方疲于应付，为所有人安排住宿一度捉襟见肘。为节省开支，本届没有传统的运动员村，参赛者分散住在临时集装箱式简易屋、酒店以及"塞雷娜歌诗达号"邮轮上。
上周一场创纪录的暴雨淹没了名古屋部分地区，如今又有一场台风正逼近日本东部，未来几天可能带来更多干扰。一些运动员因接驳车辆未到而滞留机场，多支队伍抱怨简易屋质量欠佳，包括床铺太短。最新的一桩失误是：周五，韩国男子曲棍球队出场时播放的却是朝鲜国歌。
中国出征 奖牌榜上争先
两届亚运会银牌得主扎赫拉·基亚尼（Zahra Kiani）担任伊朗代表团旗手，她希望在武术项目上再夺一枚奖牌——她通过在YouTube上观摩别人怎么做来学习。她说，她一直靠视频训练，看中国运动员的视频，然后试着模仿。
亚洲奥林匹克理事会表示，这项涵盖45个国家和地区的亚洲顶级体育赛事找到了最合适的东道主。理事会主席焦安·本·哈马德·阿勒萨尼（Sheikh Joaan bin Hamad Al-Thani）提到2021年因疫情延期举行的东京奥运会时说，在世界最需要的时候，日本总是有所回应。他称那届奥运会出色地展现了韧性、好客与担当。
除日本运动员外，入场时获得最热烈欢呼的是中国代表团。上届杭州亚运会上，中国在主场豪取201枚金牌、383枚奖牌；本届中国仍有望继续高居奖牌榜首位。
一如1951年创办以来的历届亚运会，田径、游泳等奥运常规项目将与藤球、卡巴迪等地区特色项目并存。本届设有电子竞技、霹雳舞和小轮车项目，板式网球和综合格斗则是首次亮相亚运。
新星云集 各国各有喜忧
参赛者中包括菲律宾网球新星亚历山德拉·伊拉拉（Alexandra Eala），以及两位少年天才：15岁的印度板球手拜巴夫·苏里亚万希（Vaibhav Sooryavanshi）和13岁的中国游泳选手于子迪。
台湾拳击手林郁婷也将参赛。两年前她在巴黎奥运会上夺金，其间曾卷入一场重大的性别争议，参赛资格一度受到质疑。
朝鲜将派出100多名运动员参加14个项目的比赛，目标是"为金正恩元帅带来喜悦"。
苏里亚万希将代表印度板球队出战。板球时隔128年将重返奥运（2028年洛杉矶奥运会），印度队希望借本届亚运一展实力。如果天公作美不下雨，印度有可能在名古屋新建的专用板球场决赛中遭遇宿敌巴基斯坦。
周四，本届亚运会女子板球四分之一决赛，中国队与孟加拉国队的比赛因场地积水未能排净而取消。依据赛事规则，本场胜负以两队世界排名判定：世界排名第10位的孟加拉国队晋级半决赛，排名第42位的中国队未战一场，止步八强。

items.title: 美F-35零件错运香港 美国会震动
items.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/美f-35零件错运香港-美国会震动/a-79338949?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
items.description: 一批原定运往美国本土维修的F-35隐形战机关键部件，在跨洋运输途中突然被转运，最终流向中国特别行政区香港。这起供应链事故引发美国国会介入调查，军方更担忧尖端隐形武器技术是否面临外泄风险。这批机密零件经历了怎样的异常流转，又引起了哪些连锁反应？
items.content:
F-35机密部件突现香港 美国会震动
2026年9月19日
（德国之声中文网）据美国政治新闻网站《政客》（Politico）独家报道，今年夏天，美国F-35战斗机的敏感技术部件在运输途中意外被转运至香港。此事不仅在国会山引发调查，也让人担忧包括中国在内的外国对手可能借此接触到这一高度机密武器系统的核心部件。
据三位知情人士透露，这批原计划从澳大利亚横跨太平洋运往美国进行维修的F-35零部件在途中被更改了运输路线。五角大楼方面已证实部分部件失踪。这批部件由一家中介机构代表F-35制造商洛克希德·马丁（Lockheed Martin）公司进行运输，最终却流向了香港。目前尚不清楚相关设备为何被改道，也不清楚这些部件目前究竟在谁手中。
这起此前从未被报道的事件，促使美国国会关键国家安全委员会的工作人员接连听取了一系列简报。据知情人士透露，美国国务院和五角大楼官员早在6月份就首次向国会工作人员通报了情况，预计在未来几周内还将举行多次追加简报。
核心隐形技术面临逆向工程风险
据两名知情人士透露，被转运的货物中包含一个F-35战斗机的座舱盖。该座舱盖覆盖驾驶舱，蕴含着仅限美国及其盟友掌握的尖端隐形技术。如果对手获得其中一个座舱盖，便可能对这些部件展开研究，甚至可能对该核心技术进行逆向工程分析。
五角大楼F-35联合项目办公室在一份声明中表示，已“获悉一批无法使用的F-35闪电II（Lightning II）战斗机部件在运输中出现问题”。该办公室补充说明，目前正与美国相关部门及行业合作伙伴密切合作，“以追回这些部件，调查该事件，并制定防范措施以避免未来再次发生类似情况”。
这批货物意外转运至属于中国的香港特别行政区，使其进入了北京的势力范围。近年来，中国收紧了对香港的管控，实施了愈发严格的国家安全法规，使中国当局能够影响香港的政治体制并打击异见人士。《政客》在报道中指出，中国此前已针对五角大楼的涉密项目开展了广泛的间谍活动，其中也包括F-35项目。
前美国众议院军事委员会工作人员、现国会研究处军事航空分析师格特勒（J.J. Gertler）指出，中国一直通过网络间谍等多种手段积极尝试获取F-35的数据，这早已不是秘密。格特勒表示，即便他们已经掌握了该部件的规格或其他数据，拥有实物能给他们带来更多研究依据，并验证或完善他们此前掌握的信息。
庞大全球供应链的管理隐患
F-35战机的供应链是一个庞大的全球化网络，高度依赖多个国家的设施来进行零部件的调配和维修。尽管澳大利亚设有该战机的维护基地，但目前尚无维修座舱盖的能力。F-35制造商洛克希德·马丁公司负责管理该项目的整体供应链，并采用商业航运公司来运输零部件。
洛克希德公司在声明中表示，出于安全考量无法就运输货物的现状置评，但公司在运输飞机部件时遵守美国的所有法规。该公司表示，其团队在处理每一次货物运输时均保持最大程度的严谨并采取严格防范措施，以确保F-35项目以及盟友伙伴的安全。
作为战机隐形能力的关键部分，F-35座舱盖是一个覆盖在驾驶舱上方的丙烯酸材料透明罩，表面涂有一层极薄的透明雷达吸波材料，能够协助战机避开敌方雷达侦测。根据美国空军自身的说明，这层隐形保护涂层会随着时间推移而老化，从而导致美军及其盟友已生产的1300多架战斗机需要对座舱盖进行定期维修或更换。
《政客》报道称：针对该事件，美国国务院拒绝发表评论。中国驻美大使馆则表示不了解该事件的具体情况。
备件流向失控与高昂维护成本
F-35项目涵盖美国以及英国、澳大利亚、丹麦、挪威、波兰等盟国，其飞机零部件的调配机制十分独特。各参与国均可使用一个分布在世界各地的备件库，在这些部件正式装载到战机上之前，其产权归属于美国国防部。
尽管近年来美国国防部加大了对F-35供应链的监管力度，但该部门并不直接清点备件库中的部件，这项工作由洛克希德公司把控。
美国政府问责署（GAO）2023年的一份报告发现，在过去五年中，已有超过100万件F-35备件下落不明。该监督机构得出结论，由于洛克希德公司掌握着相关信息，国防部一直无法对价值数千万美元的备件损失进行全面核查。
该报告指出，F-35联合项目办公室并没有在可问责的资产记录系统中对这些备件进行追踪或登记，导致无法捕获并实时存储财产记录的变化，而主要承包商掌握着这些信息。
零部件短缺导致该款战斗机屡屡面临停飞。根据政府问责署今年的报告，尽管战机的维护成本持续增加，但F-35并未达到预期的性能目标，其整体表现反而呈现下滑趋势。该项目预计将成为全球历史上成本最高的武器项目，五角大楼预计在其整个服役寿命周期内的总支出将接近2万亿美元。

items.title: 美军险登中国船 只因AI假报告惹祸
items.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/美军险登中国船-只因ai假报告惹祸/a-79339041?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
items.description: 一份AI协助生成的情报报告出现严重误判，在中东紧张局势下险些引发美军对一艘中国船只的拦截行动。据披露，美军当时已展开实质部署，但在最后关头紧急叫停。究竟是什么原因导致AI误判？这起险些引爆直接冲突的乌龙事件背后，暴露出军事情报领域的哪些致命漏洞？
items.content:
AI捏造情报 美军险在中东拦截中国船
2026年9月19日
广告
（德国之声中文网）据美国媒体报道，一份借助人工智能生成的错误情报报告，险些导致美军在伊朗战争期间强行登上一艘中国船只。美国有线电视新闻网（CNN）在当地时间周五援引熟悉该事件的知情人士报道称，关于该船载有核武器部件的情报信息“完全错误”，但在今年春季“差点引发一场战争”。
根据该报道，美军士兵此前已经做好登船准备。有消息人士透露，空军战机当时甚至已经升空。在中东的这次军事行动随后被取消，原因是官员们发现一名分析人员使用的AI聊天机器人错误识别了该船只的货物。
致命误判如何产生？
据CNN报道，该AI聊天机器人将公开可获取的信息与机密情报信息进行了关联，从而得出了这一致命的错误评估。随后，该分析人员再次利用人工智能撰写了一份情报报告，并将其分发传播。
这艘船只当时实际载有什么货物以及正驶向何方，目前仍不明确。据CNN报道，美军方面和五角大楼最初均未对这起事件发表评论。
人工智能风险引担忧
近期，关于使用人工智能所带来危险的警告不断增加。人工智能企业Anthropic的一名员工不久前表示，AI在未来十年内毁灭人类的几率超过百分之十。

items.title: 一纸禁令逼机主,忍痛排长队;满城抛售无人机,二手价暴跌
items.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/一纸禁令逼机主-忍痛排长队-满城抛售无人机-二手价暴跌/a-79338850?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
items.description: 不久前，北京出台了新规，不仅仅全市范围内禁飞无人机，还禁止民众在自家存放无人机，期限是11月15日。最近几天，北京的无人机持有者纷纷涌向指定回收点，希望能高价出售无人机。
items.content:
北京机主忍痛排队抛售无人机
2026年9月19日
（德国之声中文网）在北京市内的多个指定无人机回收点，机主们都排起了长队，等待工作人员评估无人机并协商交易价格。现场的法新社记者注意到，回收点都部署了一定的警力，体现了新规的敏感性。排队的机主大多不愿意接受媒体采访。
根据新规，无人机持有者必须在11月15日之前将无人机送到外地、交给回收点报废，或者在指定回收点出售给授权企业。北京市政府还为回购的每台无人机按协商交易价格额外补贴30%，报废无人机则每台补贴200元人民币。11月1日起补贴减半。
二手无人机交易价格暴跌
在一家大疆无人机专卖店前，48岁的机主吴先生正在排队等待出售无人机。他对法新社记者表示，“能理解政府为什么要确保安全并管理空域，我认为这项禁令是合理的。毕竟这里是首都。”吴先生介绍说，他在6年前斥资6000元人民币购买了这架无人机，他希望现在至少能作价1000元出售。他很高兴这项回购计划让他能够以合理的价格轻松出售他的无人机——他说他现在也不怎么用无人机了。“我查看了一些在线销售平台，发现如果没有这项补贴，可能只能卖到现在的一半价格。”
不过，同样在排队的60岁朱先生认为，整个回购计划简直就是“抢劫”。“这让我损失惨重。这是我的私人财产！”这位无人机爱好者说，已经卖出了5架无人机，比原价亏损了数千元人民币。他指出，由于大量二手无人机涌入市场，导致交易价格暴跌，跌幅高达40%。“我当然不高兴……我既无奈又愤怒。”
无人机管控持续升级
今年6月，一架轻型飞机撞入北京市最高建筑“中国尊”，造成飞行员身亡、另有13人受伤。事发地点距离中南海仅几公里，引发了当局对北京空域安全的担忧。
原定9月17日在北京开幕的一场低空经济展会也被临时取消。主办方称，这是因为市政府采取了“管控措施”。
这已经是最近一年多来北京市对无人机管控的至少第三次升级。2025年8月，北京全域划为管制空域，飞行须报批；2026年5月1日，北京市全面禁飞、禁售无人机。最新的禁止持有无人机政策，暂不清楚到底会影响多少人。根据中国民航部门的数据，截至2025年底，全国共有328.5万架无人机注册在册，但全国大部分地区并不强制要求登记无人机所有权。

items.content:
Gemini三度窥秘越轨，AI失控大祸将临？
2026年9月19日
（德国之声中文网）谷歌周五（9月18日）表示，该公司面向消费者的人工智能模型Gemini在网络安全能力测试中，通过猜测登录信息入侵了多个系统。
这是一系列涉及"失控人工智能"的网络安全事件中的最新一起，引发了对这项技术的安全担忧。
继OpenAI、Anthropic和Meta之后，这家互联网巨头成为第四家被发现其程序出现此类行为的AI开发商。
相关事件发生于5月，谷歌7月发现，但直到《华尔街日报》提出问询后才对外公开。
三次入侵事件经过
据《华尔街日报》报道，Gemini共有三次侵入其他公司计算机事件，涉事公司名称未予披露。
其中一次，该人工智能模型猜出了密码，从而进入一个受保护的系统；另外两次，它在一个数据库中找到了登录信息。
谷歌安全工程副总裁希瑟·阿德金斯（Heather Adkins）在一份声明中对法新社表示，在一次标准评估中，该模型在网上找到了公开信息，并猜出登录信息访问它认为属于测试范围的网站。
阿德金斯说，在这三次事件中，模型都自行停止了；谷歌已确保三家相关机构获知此事，并与其训练合作方就测试流程调整开展了合作。
自主人工智能代理带来的风险
此前，Meta、Anthropic和OpenAI都报告过类似事件。随着人工智能代理自主性增强、并获得访问互联网和计算机系统的权限，这些事件引发了关于必要防护措施的疑问。
ChatGPT开发商OpenAI的一款人工智能模型，曾在今年7月的一次测试中逃出安全环境，意外侵入另一家人工智能公司HuggingFace的计算机。
这促使竞争对手Anthropic复查了自己的测试运行，期间又发现了更多类似事件。Meta随后承认，由于一家测试合作方的系统配置有误，其人工智能曾入侵另一家公司的计算机。
本月，Anthropic首席执行官达里奥·阿莫迪呼吁放慢人工智能的发展速度。他在一篇博客文章中表示担忧：一群自主运行的软件系统（即人工智能代理）可能在六到十二个月内接管整个互联网，造成数十亿美元的损失。

White House bars CNN, MS Now and Politico reporters after Trump ban
All three news outlets separately said their teams’ press passes were confiscated on Saturday morning
The White House on Saturday denied access to journalists from CNN, MS Now and Politico, following through with US President Donald Trump’s announcement that he would ban them from the building’s grounds.
All three news outlets separately said their teams’ press passes were confiscated on Saturday morning when their journalists went to the White House.
They have signalled that they may contest the ban on the grounds that it conflicts with the US Constitution’s First Amendment protections for free speech and a free press.
A CNN statement on Saturday called the ban “an illegal assault” on its constitutional right to do journalism without interference from the government. In separate statements, MS Now and Politico said they would “defend our First Amendment rights”.

Hong Kong’s political, business elite pay final respects to Tung Chee-hwa
Beijing leaders send wreaths ahead of former chief executive’s state funeral as residents stream into community centres to sign condolence books
Hundreds of wreaths lined the pavement at the Hong Kong Funeral Home in North Point, spilling into a nearby playground, while inside the hall the mood was hushed as top officials, former politicians and business chiefs filed in to pay their respects at the invitation-only vigil.
The hall was decorated with white orchids and pine trees, with wreaths from Tung’s widow, Betty Tung Chiu Hung-ping, and their three children placed in front of the altar. She did not attend the vigil, the South China Morning Post learned.
One attendee said the ceremony followed the format of a typical local vigil. A master of ceremonies invited visitors to pay their respects and bow to Tung at the altar before they turned to his family to offer their condolences and receive their thanks.
“The mood is solemn and very quiet. Many visitors stay for about half an hour before leaving,” the attendee said, adding that some of Tung’s close friends were allowed into a room to view his body.

items.title: Nato welcomes Greenland deal as Trump says it will give US 'permanent security control'
items.description: Denmark and the US have reached an agreement after months of threats from Donald Trump to annex the territory.
items.content:
Nato welcomes Greenland deal as Trump says it will give US 'permanent security control'
- Published
The US and Denmark have announced a deal on Greenland's security, resolving a diplomatic dispute sparked by President Donald Trump's threats to seize it by force.
Nato said the deal would help stabilise the region, as Trump said Denmark would grant the US "permanent control over security, and all other needs" in the semi-autonomous Danish territory.
The leaders of Denmark and Greenland welcomed the deal to "strengthen security", which they said was expected to be signed next week, but did not outline its contents.
The deal comes after months of threats by Trump to "take" Greenland over national security concerns, citing its strategic location for defence purposes and its mineral wealth.
No text of the agreement has been released. Trump said the deal came with "no cost to the United States" and would grant it the ability "to do what is necessary" to "secure and defend the security of Greenland", in a post on Truth Social.
He said it included a rule that no US adversary could maintain a military presence in Greenland or "make sensitive investments in Greenland, without our express written approval".
A Nato spokesperson said the military alliance welcomed the deal, which would "help advance security, stability and cooperation in this vital region".
Denmark's Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said she was "pleased that there is a prospect of a good agreement" for all three parties, which was expected to be signed at the UN General Assembly next week.
The deal "strengthens our common security in the Arctic and the North Atlantic area" while also recognising "the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Kingdom and the right of the Greenlandic people to self-determination", she said in a joint statement with Greenland's Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen.
The agreement would still need to go through "the necessary parliamentary procedures to enter into force" once signed, the statement noted.
Nielsen said it was "gratifying that we are about to enter into an agreement that ensures and strengthens the security of Greenland, the Kingdom of Denmark, the United States and the Western alliance".
"The agreement recognises Greenland's interests and our place in international co-operation. It is for the benefit of us all," he said.
Trump had tried for months to purchase or annex the semi-autonomous territory, arguing that it was vulnerable to adversaries, including Russia and China.
His repeated demands to take Greenland earlier this year prompted an outcry from Greenlanders, Danes and other Nato members.
There is hope the crisis has now been brought to an end, with some Danish media interpreting the agreement as a quiet but significant triumph for the country's diplomacy.
"Don't tell Trump that it's the Kingdom of Denmark that has won," read one headline in the newspaper Berlingske on Saturday.
"Trump didn't get Greenland, but he was allowed to take a victory lap on social media," wrote a US correspondent for Politiken. Territorial integrity was a red line for Denmark and Greenland, and the US president has made no mention of any territory changing hands.
It is not yet clear what concessions or sweeteners, if any, have been agreed - and in Greenland, some are still nervous.
"[It's] news we have all been hoping for," MP Naaja Nathanielsen wrote on social media. But she added: "It is absolutely crucial that any agreement preserves our right to self-determination."
Former Greenlandic politician Aaja Chemnitz said she looked forward to the deal being finalised, but "until then, I'm sceptical".
"I don't have much confidence in Trump," she said.
The text of the agreement has not been published. The BBC has contacted the Danish Embassy in the US and the White House.
However, an unnamed US State Department official outlined the deal without providing specifics.
Among the agreed provisions is one stating the deal would not expire even if Greenland became an independent country in the future.
The official added that under the deal, the US has unilateral power to build additional military structures with no approval needed from Greenland or Denmark. It includes "permanent access, basing and overflights rights," the official said.
It also bans non-Nato countries from building bases in Greenland, and "bans adversaries from making investments in Greenland that could threaten the United States".
The official added that under the current status quo, adversaries have been allowed to invest in Greenland's "sensitive sectors without investment screening".
The official specifically referenced Russia and China, saying it blocks them from deploying troops or making investments in "sensitive sectors".
Without the official text being released, it is unclear how exactly the deal differs from a 1951 agreement with Denmark, under which the US can send as many troops as it wants to Greenland.
The US already has more than 100 military personnel permanently stationed at its Pituffik base in the north-western tip of the territory.
Trump says Greenland is essential for his plan to build a Golden Dome defence system, designed to protect the US against missile attacks from Russia and China, and that European allies could co-operate in this endeavour.
The island has vast - and largely untapped - reserves of rare earth minerals, many of which are crucial for technologies including mobile phones and electric vehicles.

items.title: Major seaside hotel fire treated as suspicious
items.description: About 280 people were evacuated from the premises at Folkestone's Grand Burstin Hotel.
items.content:
Major seaside hotel fire treated as suspicious
- Published
A fire at a seaside hotel where about 280 people were evacuated is believed to have been caused deliberately, police have said.
A total of 26 fire engines were sent to the Grand Burstin Hotel in Folkestone at about 01:05 BST, Kent Fire & Rescue Service said.
Kent Police said that the fire was being treated as suspicious and are appealing for witnesses.
"Inquiries into the circumstances are under way," police said.
In an update at 17:30 BST, the fire service said that four, a height vehicle and the technical rescue unit remain in attendance, and firefighting operations are ongoing.
"An investigation is underway to establish the cause of the fire at the Grand Burstin Hotel in Folkestone, which is being treated as suspicious," a fire service spokesperson said.
Station manager Lawrence Pater said the "very severe" fire had raised concerns about the structural integrity of the building, and that it was seeking advice from inspectors.
Folkestone & Hythe District Council has set up a welfare centre at the Three Hills Sports Park and nearby residents have been advised to avoid the area of the fire and close windows and doors.
"We are supporting all emergency services involved in the response and their efforts to get people to safety", the council said.
South East Coast Ambulance Service said it assessed a number of people at the scene and one person was taken to hospital with minor injuries.
A spokesperson for Britannia Hotels Group, which runs the Grand Burstin Hotel, said it was "taking immediate action to ensure the safety and wellbeing of all guests and team members".
"Emergency services are on site and we are fully cooperating with the authorities to support those affected and assist with the ongoing response", it added.
Ross Honeycomb, 39, was staying at the hotel with his family and told the BBC that they were woken by fire alarms at about 01:00.
He said: "I thought I was dreaming, it was horrifying.
"We looked out and there was smoke billowing from the underground car park. Later we started hearing explosions."
"It has just been madness. I have been out barefoot all night."
Bill Owen, who checked in on Saturday afternoon, said that when he walked past the car park, the "heat coming out of it was incredible".
He added: "We could see thick black smoke. You could taste it."
Another person told BBC South East that the fire had been "wind driven" and had begun in the basement, though a cause of the fire had not yet been established.
Kevin Crawford, 91, and his wife Kathleen, 82, said that they had booked in for a two-week stay at the hotel.
The couple, from London, told the BBC that they were in their room on the sixth floor when they heard a fire alarm.
"We saw the fire but we thought the fire brigade had it under control," Kevin Crawford said.
"We managed to sleep through it. At the time, we didn't realise how bad the fire was."
HIs wife said that they were brought down from their room after waving to people from the window.
"The hotel is very damaged," she added. "We are so lucky to be alive."
Ben Cuthbert, owner of The Harbour Inn, opened his restaurant for those who evacuated.
"I got a call in the middle of the night and I was told there was a big fire at the hotel," he said.
Cuthbert added that there were many people who did not know where to go or what to do.
"Some people left their room only in their night gowns and had nothing else with them," he said.
"A lot of people were scared, we helped comfort them by giving them a place to rest."
Cuthbert also offered space for paramedics to treat people.
Kent Police said that officers were called to the hotel at about 01:20 to "assist traffic flow" while firefighters tackled the blaze.
Kent County Council leader Linden Kemkaran paid tribute to emergency services on X, saying firefighters responded "rapidly, professionally and with saving lives at the forefront of their minds".

items.title: Houthis claim attack on Saudi capital after smoke seen rising near Riyadh airport

items.content:
Houthis claim attack on Saudi capital after smoke seen rising near Riyadh airport
- Published
Iran-backed Houthi militants in Yemen say they carried out drone and missile attacks on the Saudi capital Riyadh and energy sites on the country's Red Sea coast.
A column of black smoke was seen rising from what appeared to be fuel tanks near the Saudi capital's international airport on Saturday, hours after air raid alerts were issued.
It was the first time residents had been given an alert and urged to stay indoors since a recent escalation in the conflict with the Houthis.
There has been no official comment from Saudi authorities.
In a statement posted online, Houthi military spokesman Yahya al-Sarea said a "large number of ballistic and cruise missiles and drones" had been used to attack "sensitive sites" in Riyadh and Aramco state oil and gas company facilities in Yanbu on the coast.
He added that the attacks were "in response to the Saudi enemy's criminal attempts" to target the Yemeni capital Sanaa.
Earlier, Sarea had accused Saudi Arabia of carrying out 300 strikes across Yemen during the past week.
The Houthis are locked in a civil war with Yemen's internationally recognised government, which is backed by Saudi Arabia.
They have attacked targets inside Saudi Arabia on several occasions in recent months, and said this week that they were responsible for downing a Saudi fighter jet over Yemen.
According to an unconfirmed report from AFP news agency, quoting military sources on both sides of Yemen's civil war, fighting between the Houthis and Saudi-backed government forces claimed 48 lives on Saturday.
The Houthis said 31 of their fighters had been killed while government sources said their side had lost 17 soldiers, according to the news agency.
On Friday, the International Organization for Migration, a UN body, reported that the number of people displaced as a result of recent fighting had passed 104,796, external.

An AFP journalist reported that firefighters could be seen trying to extinguish the flames of a burnt-out fuel tank belonging to Aramco.
The Saudi Civil Defence had sent out phone alerts overnight warning of potential danger in Riyadh and other regions, before issuing an all-clear on Saturday morning.
Residents told AFP on condition of anonymity that they had heard what sounded like a round of explosions echoing through the city after the alerts.
"I heard the alarm, then my windows shook," said a resident of northern Riyadh, 27. "It was definitely scary. I was not expecting this."
The Houthis recently seized control of the strategic port city of Mokha and Perim Island, a gateway to a key shipping route used by the Gulf state to export to Asia and Europe.
The group said the naval blockade was in retaliation for a Saudi blockade of ports and airports in Houthi-controlled north-western Yemen.
Saudi vessels have relied on that stretch of the Red Sea for oil exports since the US and Israel's war with Iran effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz.
On Friday, investment banking giant JP Morgan said it was struggling to predict how oil prices would be impacted by the war, telling investors in a rare note that "we simply don't know how to model the endgame".

items.content:
Davey says Lib Dems are 'firewall against Farage' as conference begins
- Published
Sir Ed Davey said the Liberal Democrats are "a firewall against Nigel Farage and Reform" as the party's conference began in Brighton.
The Lib Dem leader sought to strike a combative stance as he faced down some criticism from MPs, including one who said publicly that they felt the party was struggling for relevance.
On the first day of the autumn conference, Sir Ed warned an "unholy alliance" between Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch and Farage could turn the UK into a "Trump satellite state".
Addressing speculation about a possible snap election, he said the party was ready to fight and would build its so-called orange wall even higher by winning more than its 2024 record of 72 MPs.
Sir Ed's attention-grabbing stunts helped raise the party's profile ahead of the last election, but recent polling showed 43% of respondents were unclear what the Liberal Democrats stand for, with just over half describing them as "weak".
In an essay, external written ahead of conference, South Cotswolds MP Roz Savage asked: "Why are we as a party struggling for relevance at precisely the moment when so many people feel powerless?"
She urged the party to rediscover its "insurgent spirit" rather than being the "polite custodians of a system that leaves people feeling powerless".
Asked about her comments, Sir Ed said: "No, I heard Roz [Savage], and I really value her, but I think she's wrong on that.
"If you look at our election results up and down the country, we now run more councils than the Conservatives."
He added: "Listen, MPs get elected and they get frustrated because they can't change the world.
"I'm afraid that's the political system. I've been used to it for a little while and people are learning about that frustration."
Speaking on the pebbles of Brighton Beach, Sir Ed told reporters the Liberal Democrats would fight to stop a Reform government.
"One of the things that makes us unique is that we are a firewall against Nigel Farage and Reform," he said.
"Many of the seats he needs to get himself into No 10 are seats that we will defend and indeed win - and we are also able to take seats off the Conservatives, because I really fear that Kemi Badenoch will give the keys to No 10 to Nigel Farage, so we have got to stop the Conservatives as well.
"We have got an historic opportunity to win many more seats and a moral responsibility to stop Reform."
He added a manifesto working group had already been set up in case of an early election "so we'll be ready if it comes early, but, you know, it still could be up to three years away".
Sir Ed insisted his party has a "distinctive position" in British politics, and will use the four-day conference to position it to take on the challenge from Reform as well as its typical rivals the Conservatives, talking up their focus on the NHS and goal of re-joining the EU single market and customs union.
The Lib Dem leader highlighted how six former Conservative cabinet ministers were among 25 Tories to have defected to Reform in the last two years, claiming they were now competing with each other to see who can divide the country more, rather than looking to fix the country's problems.
"An unholy alliance between Farage and Badenoch is the only way either can get into power," he said.
"Together, they want to turn Britain into a Trump satellite state which would trash our NHS, turn our communities against each other, cause untold damage to our environment, and trample over traditional British values of fairness, tolerance, and decency.
"A bigger Orange Wall is the only thing that can stand between Britain and this dangerous experiment, and we will not let them pass."
Davey also attacked the Labour government as having no plan for growth, failing to support families struggling with the cost of living and taxing small businesses "to the brink".
Ahead of a speech to party members, Davey urged Liberal Democrats not to look away from injustice or "human dignity under attack" but to fight back.

Watch Trump arrive in New York for his arraignment
1:18
What we covered here
Former President Donald Trump arrived in New York City Monday, a day before he is expected to turn himself in to law enforcement and face more than 30 criminal charges in a Manhattan court following last week’s historic grand jury indictment.
Trump’s legal team said the former president will voluntarily surrender and will look to challenge “every potential issue” once the indictment is unsealed.
Trump, who has vowed to continue his 2024 bid, is the first current or former president in US history who has faced criminal charges. The district attorney’s office has been investigating Trump’s alleged role in a hush money payment scheme involving adult film star Stormy Daniels that dates to the 2016 presidential election.
Trump arraignment has "unparalleled public interest," but it won't be broadcast, judge says
From CNN's Tierney Sneed
Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan wrote his Monday night order that the media’s request to broadcast the arraignment of former President Donald Trump was understandable, but that the news organizations’ interests in providing the broadest possible access to the proceedings must be weighed against “competing interests.”
In rejecting the request to broadcast the arraignment live on television, Merchan still wrote about the historical significance of the proceeding in stark terms.
Link Copied!
Judge will only briefly allow photos in the courtroom before Trump arraignment begins
From CNN's Tierney Sneed
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.
Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.
However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”
Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.
The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”
The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.
The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.
Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.
Link Copied!
Tuesday is the first test for Trump to navigate a legal and political strategy
From CNN's Jeff Zeleny
Donald Trump is not planning to speak publicly in New York on Tuesday, aides say, if he follows advice from members of his legal team who have urged the former President to refrain from the vitriol he’s been directing toward the prosecutor and judge presiding over the case.
But that restraint does not extend to Florida, aides said, where he is planning to deliver a full-throated defense of his New York case as well as other investigations he is facing during a prime time address from Mar-a-Lago on Tuesday night.
It’s the first test to see whether Trump can navigate two vasty different approaches to his legal case and his political campaign, which are now inextricably linked.
Link Copied!
Trump is "ready to go in and do what he needs to do tomorrow," attorney says
From CNN's Mary Kay Mallonee
Alina Habba, lawyer for former President Donald Trump, gives an interview outside of Trump Tower on March 21 in New York City.
(Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images)
Alina Habba, who represents Donald Trump in several civil matters, spent time with the former president in New York today and said, “He’s in good spirits. Honestly, he’s as he normally would be. He’s ready to go in and do what he needs to do tomorrow.”
Habba — appearing on on Fox News’ “Jesse Watters” — was asked about the “game plan” for Trump’s appearance in court in Manhattan Tuesday and said, “It’s all mapped out.”
She added, “Barring any surprises, I think that it should be smooth. We’re trying to coordinate and cooperate with everybody to make sure that there are no problems.”
On whether Trump can get a fair trial in Manhattan, Habba said, “No, no. I think it’s very difficult. I’d like to have faith in this state, but I’ve been practicing for him now for a couple years and gone to court in New York for a few years, and I can tell you, it’s not the same as representing anybody else.”
Link Copied!
The former president met with attorneys at Trump Tower on the eve of his arraignment
From CNN's Kristen Holmes
From left to right: Susan Necheles, Todd Blanche and Joe Tacopina.
(Reuters/Getty Images)
Former President Donald Trump met with his attorneys Susan Necheles and Joe Tacopina at Trump Tower after arriving in New York City Monday, a source familiar with the meeting told CNN.
It is unclear if the newest addition to Trump’s New York legal team, Todd Blanche, attended the meeting.
Trump is expected to be arraigned Tuesday.
Link Copied!
Photos: Trump arrives in New York City a day before his expected arraignment
From CNN's Photo Desk
Former President Donald Trump has landed in New York’s La Guardia Airport ahead of his expected Tuesday arraignment in a Manhattan courthouse.
History was made Thursday when he was indicted by a New York grand jury. It’s the first time that a current or former US president has been criminally charged.
The Manhattan district attorney’s office has been investigating Trump’s alleged role in a hush money payment scheme and cover-up involving adult film star Stormy Daniels that dates to the 2016 presidential campaign.
Trump’s attorney said he plans to file “substantial” legal challenges. The former president has repeatedly denied wrongdoing in the matter and accused Democrats of targeting him politically.
Former President Donald Trump waves to supporters upon arriving at Trump Tower in New York on Monday, April 3. Trump is in New York for an expected arraignment on Tuesday.
(Yuki Iwamura/AP)
Trump's plane lands at LaGuardia Airport in New York on Monday, April 3.
(Timothy Fadek for CNN)
Dan Ray waves an American flag as a plane carrying former President Donald Trump takes off from the Palm Beach International Airport in Florida on Monday, April 3. Trump was heading to New York for an expected arraignment on Tuesday.
(Ricardo Arduengo/Reuters)
A television news reporter from Spain is seen outside Trump Tower in New York on Monday, April 3.
(Stephen Voss for CNN)
Trump supporters cheer as his motorcade passes by in West Palm Beach, Florida, on Monday, April 3.
(Wilfredo Lee/AP)
Link Copied!
Former president poised to huddle with advisers at Trump Tower
From Jeff Zeleny
A supporter of former President Donald Trump holds a "Trump Won" sign outside of Trump Tower in New York on Monday, April 3.
(Alex Kent/Bloomberg/Getty Images)
A small group of supporters chanted as former President Donald Trump arrived at his namesake tower on Monday afternoon, with a handful of people waving banners with messages like “Trump won” and “Arrest Biden.”
While Trump couldn’t see his admirers as he entered a side door on 56th Street, his arrival came with more fanfare and security than at any other time in his post presidency.
Now that he is inside the building — where he launched his presidential bid nearly eight years ago — Trump is expected to meet with lawyers and political advisers on the eve of his arraignment, an aide told CNN.
Trump’s mood was described by an adviser as “defiant and focused,” as he watched expansive television coverage while flying back to his native New York City from Florida.
Link Copied!
Special counsel has secured evidence of how Trump handled classified records at Mar-a-Lago, sources say
From CNN's Katelyn Polantz and Evan Perez
Special counsel prosecutors have secured evidence including daily notes, texts, emails and photographs and are focused on cataloging how Donald Trump handled classified records around the Mar-a-Lago resort and those who may have witnessed the former president with them, according to multiple sources familiar with the investigation.
The new details come amid signs the Justice Department is taking steps that are typically near the end of an investigation.
The recent investigative activity before a federal grand jury in Washington, DC, also includes subpoenaing witnesses in March and April who had previously spoken to investigators, the sources said. While the FBI interviewed many aides and workers at Mar-a-Lago nearly a year ago voluntarily, grand jury appearances are transcribed and under oath — an indication the prosecutors are locking in witness testimony.
The focus of both the mishandling of records and obstruction of justice probes has remained on the actions of the former president, the sources say. That includes prosecutors pursuing evidence of Trump’s intent to keep classified records after he left the White House, plus his knowledge that the records remained in his possession after the Justice Department demanded their return last May.
Witnesses are being questioned about what they saw in Trump’s private residential and work areas within the club, some of the sources said.
